Run the ADBuddy host in this terminal. It classifies every adb command the agent
runs, journals it, shows it here and asks you before anything irreversible.
It also starts the agent; `--no-agent` runs only the host, and you start the agent
yourself in another terminal with `adbuddy run`.

Usage:
  adbuddy serve [flags]

Examples:
  adbuddy serve
  adbuddy serve --adb ~/platform-tools/adb --serial adb-XXXX-yyyy._adb-tls-connect._tcp
  adbuddy serve --json > journal.ndjson

Flags:
      --adb string         path to the real adb (default: adb_path in config.toml, else the adb installed by adbuddy setup)
      --confirm string     where to confirm 🔴 commands when the phone app is not connected: auto (this terminal if its input is interactive, else deny), terminal (reads standard input even if it is not a terminal, such as a pipe) or deny (default "auto")
      --effort string      effort Claude Code uses: low, medium, high, xhigh or max (default: agent_effort in config.toml, else low; inherit = your own)
  -h, --help               help for serve
      --model string       model Claude Code uses (--model; default: agent_model in config.toml, else claude-haiku-5-5; inherit = the one you set in Claude Code)
      --no-agent           do not start the agent here: run it yourself with 'adbuddy run' (no chat from the phone)
      --serial string      the phone to use when several are connected
      --workspace string   agent environment (default: workspace in config.toml, else ~/ADBuddy/default)

Global Flags:
      --json   machine-readable JSON output, for the commands that support it
